title: Lesson 10 - Programmatic: with/without sharing, runAs, User vs System Mode, When Apex Sharing Is Needed
description: Given a scenario, recommend the appropriate programmatic solution (with/without sharing, runAs, user vs system mode) and determine when Apex sharing is required.

questions.question: A batch job must modify records owned by users across many divisions, regardless of ownership, using a queueable that runs as the system. Which class declaration is appropriate and why?
options: 'without sharing' (or default system mode) because the operation is platform-context and must ignore record ownership
A permission set with View All
questions.explanation: A platform-triggered queueable that must act across ownership boundaries runs in system mode, which ignores record-level sharing. 'with sharing' would restrict it, and permissions/runAs do not change system-mode processing.

questions.question: What does System.runAs(testUser) accomplish in a test?
options: It runs the code as testUser so you can assert that user's effective record and field access
It only works on the system user
questions.explanation: runAs changes the running user within the test so you can verify the security model from that user's perspective. It does not disable sharing, grant permissions, or require the system user.

questions.question: When is Apex Managed Sharing the correct tool rather than a sharing rule?
options: When the access criteria are too complex or dynamic for a criteria-based sharing rule
When you need to grant object-level permissions
When you want to restrict access
questions.explanation: Managed Sharing is for complex/dynamic record grants the declarative sharing model cannot express. It grants record access, never object permissions, and cannot restrict.
